transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Recording: internal link (shared)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neal (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Arcadia Head Infra), Sofia Alvarez (Arcadia Sec Arch), Ethan Brooks (Arcadia Compliance), Marta Klein (Arcadia NetOps)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
- Deep dive on private deployment secure posture: network segmentation, inbound controls, egress restrictions, firewall ops, and audit log retention for SOC2/ISO readiness.
- Discussed RBAC + SAML SSO mapping, KMS/HSM integration patterns, and audit artifact collection.
- Agreed on runbook share, network diagram, firewall ruleset, and lab test for latency.

Topics:
- VPC segmentation vs physical air-gap tradeoffs
- Perimeter firewall rules and ephemeral ingress proxies
- Egress allow-listing and egress proxy architecture
- Audit logs: retention, hashing, and offsite storage for SOC two/ISO 27001
- KMS integration patterns (bring-your-own-key), HSM options, and key rotation cadence
- RBAC mapping to Arcadia IAM via SAML / SCIM

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call — we'll cover network segmentation, firewall ops, and what artifacts you need for SOC two. Priya is going to walk through our suggested topology and rules.
[00:18] Ravi: Sounds good, thanks Maya. we're mostly concerned about two things: 1) isolation from our public services and 2) proving to auditors that logs and keys are controlled.
[00:28] Priya: Cool, I'll start with a high level diagram. so in the private deployment we recommend a three-zone model — management plane, inference plane, and storage plane. each is in its own V P C or subnet; traffic between them is only via controlled L4/L7 proxies.
[00:46] Marta: when you say V P C, you mean dedicated V P C per customer inside our colo, right? not like shared tenancy.
[00:54] Priya: correct — dedicated V P C / network segments. in colo you'd map those to separate VLANs and hypervisor security groups. we also support a fully air-gapped option for high-reg clients but that changes support SLAs.
[01:12] Sofia: okay, what's the recommended inbound pattern for model serving? we want to avoid opening wide east-west routes.
[01:20] Liam: recommended pattern is an ingress proxy at the edge — ideally a small fleet in a DMZ that terminates TLS, enforces tokens, does request shaping, and only forwards to the inference plane over mTLS. the proxy can be hosted in your perimeter and you maintain the TLS certs.
[01:38] Ethan: for auditors, they'll want proof of key custody and egress controls. how does Redwood handle K M S? do you support BYOK with our H S M?
[01:46] Priya: yes — we support BYOK via customer K M S endpoints and we can integrate with H S M-backed keys. the runtime never stores plaintext keys; we use envelope encryption. rotation cadence is configurable but we recommend 90 days for active keys, and we can present K M S access logs as part of the audit package. note: sometimes the logs look different depending on cloud provider so we normalize them in the runbook.
[02:08] [brief cross talk]
[02:20] Sofia: what about RBAC? we need to map our SAML groups to Redwood roles for dev vs ops vs compliance auditors.
[02:28] Maya: we have a mapping template — you'll push SAML assertion attributes and we map to roles (admin, operator, readonly). SCIM provisioning is supported for user lifecycle. we can also create read-only auditor roles that only get access to logs and reports.
[02:46] Ravi: good. what about the audit logs themselves — where are they stored? do you keep copies in customer-managed storage?
[02:54] Priya: two options: 1) logs streamed to your central log collector (we support syslog, S3 with server-side encryption, or APIs to ingest into SIEM), or 2) Redwood stores encrypted blobs and forwards periodic digests to your archive. for SOC two you typically want the raw events; we recommend streaming to your S3 with server-side K M S (BYOK) so you maintain custody.
[03:18] Marta: is there any chance logs could be altered if someone gets access to the runtime?
[03:24] Liam: we hash and append logs to an append-only ledger and you can replicate the digest to your archival store. that makes tampering detectable. also RBAC + MFA limits who can access runtime consoles.
[03:36] Ethan: auditors ask for retention policy and destruction policy. what are default retention windows?
[03:42] Priya: default is 90 days hot, 365 days cold — but with private deployments you control retention; we can set retention to match your policy and provide WORM snapshots if required.
[03:52] Sofia: network-level: how do we lock egress? we want to allow only certain external APIs and internal services.
[03:59] Priya: two layered model: at the hypervisor/VLAN layer you configure egress ACLs to only allow outbound to your egress proxy, and at application level Redwood enforces domain allow-lists. for example, model downloads happen from a signed artifact store and are validated by checksums and signatures.
[04:18] Ravi: about firewall rules, we have a central perimeter firewall team that manages change windows. can Redwood provide a ruleset we can drop into our change process?
[04:26] Maya: yes — Priya will share a recommended baseline ruleset (ingress/egress with port numbers, CIDR examples, and expected flow descriptions). it's intended to be copy/paste into change tickets.
[04:36] [00:05:00] Marta: latency is a concern — we need p95 under 100ms for our customer-facing flows. does the egress proxy and mTLS add measurable jitter?
[05:08] Priya: modest increase — our internal tests show ~8-12ms added at p95 for a colocated proxy, but that depends on your proxy performance. we can run a lab test in our sandbox with your sample traffic to validate.
[05:26] Sofia: about segmentation macros — can you support micro-segmentation via service mesh, or do you expect customers to do firewall ACLs?
[05:34] Liam: both. we support integration with service meshes for fine-grained L7 policies and also provide L4 ACL guidance. many customers use a mesh for intra-cluster auth and egress ACLs for external network control.
[05:46] Ethan: what about evidence for ISO 27001 controls? specifically, change management and privileged access logs.
[05:52] Priya: we provide change history for deployments, who approved it, and artifact hashes. privileged access is logged — we can export session recordings metadata (not raw video) and API calls produced by admin sessions. these are exportable for your auditors.
[06:08] Ravi: any special ops needed for formulaic snapshots for forensic?
[06:12] Priya: we can spin off snapshot archives on-demand and push to your cold store; snapshots are immutable and include checksums for binary artifacts.
[06:20] [00:10:00] Sofia: threat model question — in the event of a compromised node in the inference plane, how do we limit data exfil?
[06:30] Liam: primary controls: egress ACLs to a hardened proxy, no outbound internet from inference plane, strict RBAC to limit who can start jobs that access customer data, and encryption in transit and at rest. also we recommend red-teaming the model-serving code path.
[06:46] Marta: does Redwood support tokenization/PII scrubbing at ingress? we want an option to mask or route PII to a protected repo.
[06:54] Priya: yes — you can configure a pre-handler that strips or tokenizes fields, or route sensitive payloads to a dedicated processing queue with stricter retention. we can include that in the sandbox test.
[07:08] Maya: quick check — are there any regulatory data residency constraints? Arcadia previously mentioned EU-only for a subset of customers.
[07:16] Sofia: yes, some accounts must keep data in EU. how do you support multi-region private deployments?
[07:22] Priya: we can deploy control plane clones in region and bind inference artifacts to region-restricted storage. for strict residency we suggest dedicated private deployment in the target region — we avoid cross-region replication by policy.
[07:36] Ethan: auditors want to see access reviews. do you have an automated access review export?
[07:42] Priya: yes — monthly access reports that show active users, last login, roles, and outdated accounts flagged. we can export them as CSV or push to your compliance S3.
[07:52] Ravi: downtime scenarios — if an egress proxy misconfigures, do you have fallback with limited functionality?
[07:58] Liam: we have a degraded mode: if egress is blocked we can serve from local cached artifacts and block external model downloads; there's a fail-soft policy to preserve availability for in-flight sessions while preventing new model pulls. this is often part of the incident runbook.
[08:18] [00:20:00] Sofia: quick clarification on log integrity — you mentioned an append-only ledger. is it customer-controlled or Redwood-controlled?
[08:26] Priya: ledger is generated by Redwood but we can publish digests to your archival store (so you control the authoritative copy of digests). that way the ledger exists internally but tamper evidence is external.
[08:36] Ethan: about SSO — do you support multiple SAML IdPs? we have separate IdPs for engineers and auditors.
[08:44] Maya: yes multiple IdPs are supported; you can configure IdP priority and map groups to roles. SCIM handles user provisioning from primary IdP.
[08:52] Ravi: can we automate rotation of keys in a zero-downtime fashion?
[08:56] Priya: yes — we use dual-key rollout: new key is staged, both keys accepted during transition, then old key retired. we can script the rotation to align with your change window.
[09:08] Marta: in terms of day-to-day ops, who handles firewall rule changes — Arcadia or Redwood?
[09:14] Maya: we recommend Arcadia operate perimeter firewalls and Redwood provide the suggested ruleset and guide for emergency rules. for internal micro-segmentation, we can operate a managed service if you prefer.
[09:26] Sofia: any example artifacts we can review? network diagram, rule templates, SOC two checklist?
[09:32] Maya: yes — I'll send a runbook zip: network diagram (PNG), baseline firewall rules (CSV), SOC two evidence list (spreadsheet), and RBAC mapping template.
[09:42] [00:40:00] Short silence and side discussion about scheduling the lab test.
[09:56] Priya: one last technical note — model KV cache behavior. you mentioned concerns about chat history stored in cache; we recommend encrypting cache shards with per-tenant keys and periodic eviction policies.
[10:12] Ravi: eviction policy — how long is cache kept? some chats are transient and we want them short.
[10:18] Priya: default is session-scoped, but you can configure TTL down to minutes. we can show the config in the sandbox.
[10:28] Ethan: finally, what will you provide as evidence to our external auditors?
[10:34] Priya: artifact bundle typically includes: network diagram, firewall baseline and change logs, RBAC mapping and access reports, K M S access logs and key rotation history, log retention and digest files, and deployment change history with approvals. we also include a short operations narrative describing controls.
[10:50] Maya: great — to recap next steps: Priya uploads ruleset, Maya will send runbook and SOC two docs, Arcadia provides subnet map and confirms audit cadence, and we'll schedule the lab latency test.
[10:58] Sofia: thanks everyone. small ask — can you mark which artifacts are redacted vs raw for auditor consumption? we prefer minimal PII in auditor copies.
[11:06] Priya: yes we'll label artifacts and provide both redacted and full copies in secure S3.
[11:12] Ravi: thanks — that covers our main concerns.
[11:16] Maya: excellent. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the lab and upload the docs to the shared workspace. thanks all.

Meeting end.

Notes about transcription quality: medium — a few product names and acronyms were auto-transcribed oddly (K M S / H S M / V P C sometimes spaced).
